special_cases: Wings (1): Won Outstanding Picture at the 1st ceremony. That night a second top prize, Unique and Artistic Picture, went to Sunrise; the Academy later dropped that award and counts Wings as the first Best Picture. Sunrise is not counted as a Best Picture nominee.
La La Land (89): Announced as the winner by mistake after the wrong envelope was handed to the presenters; Moonlight was the actual winner.
Moonlight (89): The real winner, announced minutes after La La Land was read out in error.
2nd ceremony (1928/29): no official nominees were announced; the five films are the de facto nominees the Academy later reconstructed.

oddities.title: Two top prizes, and a talkie left out
oddities.text: The first ceremony crowned Wings as Outstanding Picture and Sunrise as Unique and Artistic Picture; the second award was dropped a year later. The Jazz Singer was ruled ineligible because synchronized sound made it an unfair competitor, and received an honorary award instead.

oddities.title: The year with no nominees
oddities.text: No nominees were announced at the 2nd ceremony; The Broadway Melody simply won. The 4 other films listed today were reconstructed later by the Academy from records of what the judges had considered.

oddities.title: The trophy went to the father
oddities.text: All Quiet on the Western Front was produced by Carl Laemmle Jr., but the award was presented to his father, Carl Laemmle.
films: All Quiet on the Western Front

oddities.title: Second and third place, announced
oddities.text: For 3 ceremonies in a row (1932/33, 1934, 1935), the Academy also announced which films came second and third. Cavalcade beat A Farewell to Arms and Little Women; It Happened One Night beat The Barretts of Wimpole Street and The House of Rothschild; Mutiny on the Bounty beat The Informer and Captain Blood.

oddities.title: The wrong envelope
oddities.text: The presenters were handed a spare Best Actress envelope, so La La Land was read out as Best Picture. During the acceptance speeches, La La Land producer Jordan Horowitz, now holding the right card, announced that Moonlight had won.

oddities.label: 2020/21 and 2021
oddities.title: A 14-month year, then a 10-month one
oddities.text: The pandemic stretched eligibility for the 93rd ceremony to the end of February 2021, so Nomadland's year ran 14 months. The next year was cut to ten months (March to December 2021), and CODA won it.

oddities.label: 1927/28 to 2025
oddities.title: From 3 nominees to 12
oddities.text: The field has never had a fixed size for long: 3 films at the first ceremony, 12 in 1934 and 1935, exactly 5 for 68 ceremonies, 10 in 2009 and 2010, then 8 or 9 until 2020/21, and 10 every year since 2021.
